title: 'I Couldn't Sleep': Gondhal Director on the Anxiety Behind India's Oscar Entry
excerpt: Santosh Davakhar's debut Marathi thriller is India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards — and its director says the tight submission timeline sent him to his doctor.
body:
• Gondhal, a Marathi psychological thriller and director Santosh Davakhar's first film, is India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards.
  • Davakhar told Hindustan Times the selection left him sleepless with anxiety over the tight submission timeline — he consulted his doctor — even though he had expected the pick.
  • The film, set over one night during a traditional Gondhal ritual in rural Maharashtra, stars Ishita Deshmukh and Kishor Kadam, with music by Ilaiyaraaja.
  • It returned to Indian theatres on November 13 in seven languages; the Academy shortlist is announced December 15, nominations on January 21, and the Oscars ceremony is on March 14, 2027.

Santosh Davakhar's first film has become India's face at the Oscars — and the director says the honour kept him awake. Gondhal, his Marathi-language psychological thriller, has been chosen by the Film Federation of India as the country's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards. In an interview with Hindustan Times, reported by NDTV, Davakhar described the days after the announcement as a flood of calls about technical requirements, submissions and congratulations.

"I experienced so much anxiety over the tight timeline."

— Santosh Davakhar, director of Gondhal, to Hindustan Times

Davakhar said the anxiety was severe enough that he could not sleep and consulted his doctor. It was not doubt about the film: he said he had expected the selection before it was announced, and had posted on Instagram two days ahead of the announcement that he would not release the film on OTT for six months because he strongly felt it would be picked as India's entry. "This is my first film," he said, adding that he is learning through the whole experience.

What the film is

Gondhal is a 2025 Marathi psychological thriller, written, directed and produced by Davakhar. It is set in rural Maharashtra over a single night, during a Gondhal — a traditional night-long devotional ritual performed for a newly married couple — and follows a young bride whose schemes turn the sacred ceremony into a night of betrayal and violence. The cast includes Ishita Deshmukh, Kishor Kadam, Yogesh Sohoni, Suresh Vishwakarma, Nishad Bhoir, Anuj Prabhu and Vitthal Kale. Ilaiyaraaja composed the score, and reviewers have singled out Amalendu Chaudhary's low-light cinematography and an opening sequence reportedly shot in a single uninterrupted take of about 25 minutes. Davakhar won the Silver Peacock for Best Director at the 56th International Film Festival of India.

The campaign, and the argument around it

The film has screened in London, Manchester and Los Angeles. Davakhar said Los Angeles audiences responded particularly warmly, asking detailed questions at screenings about the characters, about why India chose this film over Bollywood titles, and about how specific character layers were written. He said films made in India's different languages deserve an equal chance to represent the country internationally, and noted that India has two films in the International Feature conversation this year — Gondhal and Theja Rio's Angh — expressing hope that one of them reaches the winning stage. The selection has also drawn public debate, including criticism from filmmaker Anurag Kashyap about the kind of Indian cinema that travels to the Oscars; Davakhar's response was to ask audiences and critics to watch the film before passing a verdict.

How to watch it

Gondhal returned to Indian theatres on November 13, 2026, re-released across seven languages, and Davakhar has said it will not go to OTT for six months — the theatrical run is the way to see it for now. For diaspora readers, the film's awards campaign is centred on Los Angeles, where it has already screened. The road ahead is set by the Academy's schedule: the International Feature shortlist is announced on December 15, 2026, nominations follow on January 21, 2027, and the 99th Academy Awards take place on March 14, 2027, in Los Angeles.
